title: Latency Focus Lens — walkthrough and playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc describes the "Latency Focus Lens" — a lightweight, temporary UI overlay and interaction pattern inside the trace viewer for quickly surfacing and comparing slow spans. The goal is to give engineers and SREs an instant, low-friction way to find the dominant latency contributors in a trace, compare sibling spans, and capture a short snapshot for runbooks or incident chat.

Why this exists / problem statement:
- Users often open a trace with a single symptom: "this request is slow". The full waterfall is dense and the signal (where time is being spent) can be obscured by many short spans, service noise, or long client-side waits.
- Current flows require too many clicks: expand spans, filter by duration, then hunt for siblings across lanes. We want a one-click lens that: highlights top N latency contributors, supports quick A/B of two spans, and can produce a compact summary (copyable) for Slack/Jira.

Primary goals (MVP):
1) Quickly surface top N spans by self-time and critical path impact (N default = 5).
2) Provide an ephemeral overlay that does not change the canonical trace state (no permanent filtering unless user confirms).
3) Enable a side-by-side compact compare mode for any two spans discovered through the lens.
4) Exportable short summary (text) with links to trace/time snippets and optional selected span IDs.

Success metrics (how we'll measure MVP):
- Time-to-first-insight: median reduction from 45s -> 15s when locating dominant span in a 300-span trace (from usability test).
- Number of clicks to capture and share a span summary: target <= 3.
- Uptake: 20% of trace opens in enterprise orgs using Console within 3 months.

Personas and common tasks:
- On-call SRE: Find the slowest downstream service in a trace and paste a short summary in PagerDuty/Slack.
- Backend dev: Compare durations and tags of two spans to validate whether a config change reduced self-time.
- Product engineer: Quickly check whether a specific operation (e.g., image-encode) is the hotspot without leaving the console.

High-level interaction flow (wireframe notes):
1) Trigger: Lens icon (magnifier with stopwatch) in trace header, hotkey "L" opens the lens.
2) Overlay: Semi-transparent panel on the right (300–420px) listing: top_contributors (ranked by critical path impact), each row shows span name, service, self-time, total-time, occurrence count, and a small sparklined timeline mini-bar showing when within trace the span occurs.
3) Inline highlights: Clicking a row briefly pulses the corresponding span in the waterfall (3s) and scrolls it into view.
4) Multi-select: Cmd/Ctrl+click to pick up to 2 spans for compare. When 2 are selected, a compact compare pane appears pinned under the lens with side-by-side columns comparing duration breakdowns, tags, resource hints (container/pod id), and first/last event timestamps.
5) Snapshot & copy: Button "Copy short report" produces a 1–3 line markdown/snippet (see example below) and a link (trace ID + span IDs + time range) that can be pasted into chat or a Jira ticket.

Example short report (auto-generated):
- Trace 8a3f9b — 1230ms total
- Top contributor: span: db.query (payments-service) — self: 610ms / total: 620ms (appearance: 2)
- Second: span: image-encode (media-service) — self: 310ms / total: 325ms
- Link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/8a3f9b?spans=span-42,span-51

Wireframe details and states:
- Closed state: lens icon grey. Hover reveals tooltip: "Latency Focus Lens (L)".
- Open state: lens slides in from right; main trace remains interactive but dimmed. The overlay is keyboard navigable (up/down to move rows, Enter to pulse, space to multi-select).
- Empty state: if trace has < 3 spans, show "No dominant spans found — try full trace view" and a hint to switch to trace-level filters.
- Heavy-trace performance: overlay must calculate top N in < 200ms for traces up to 2k spans (server-side precompute is preferred, UI fallback uses approximate aggregation).

Accessibility considerations:
- High-contrast focus ring for keyboard selection.
- ARIA live region for pulse actions: screen readers should announce "Highlighting span db.query — payment-service — 610ms".
- Ensure copy-snippet button is reachable via Enter and includes a confirmation toast.

Edge cases and interactions to define:
- Duplicate span names across services: show service badge and optionally the container/pod short id.
- When a selected span is collapsed inside a parent span: pulse action should auto-expand the parent(s) enough to reveal the span (but not fully uncollapse other lanes).
- Traces with heavy client-side waits: show a small indicator if the top contributor is a "client wait" (http:wait or network-wait) to avoid misattributing server work.
- When multiple occurrences of the same span exist, rows should list occurrence count and allow "jump to next/prev occurrence" controls.

Backlog / grooming items (candidate tickets):
- TR-942: Frontend: lens UI skeleton + slide-in panel, keyboard navigation (priority P0).
- TR-943: Backend: top-N span aggregator endpoint (cacheable per trace) with critical-path ranking (priority P0).
- TR-944: Snapshot generator + link shortener (priority P1).
- TR-945: Compare pane layout and tag diffing (priority P1).
- TR-946: Accessibility audit & screenreader fixes (priority P2).
- TR-947: UX polish: sparklines and occurrence jump controls (priority P2).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Lens opens with hotkey and lists top 5 contributors for sample traces (unit + integration tests).
- Pulse action scrolls and highlights the span in the waterfall reliably in 95% of test traces.
- Copy short report contains trace link and the top 2 spans with durations.
- Backend top-N endpoint responds within 200ms for traces up to 2000 spans in load test.

Open design questions (need product + engineering decisions):
- Default ranking metric: pure self-time vs. critical-path impact? Proposal: primary = critical-path, secondary = self-time. Need agreement for rollout.
- Should lens selections persist across trace sessions? Currently designed ephemeral; consider a toggle to persist for saved views.
- Permissions: should copy-link include short-lived tokens for private traces when shared externally? Security/PM to advise.

Prototype notes (for design handoff):
- Export Zeplin/figma frames: 3 states (closed, open listing, open compare) with annotated interactions.
- Provide microcopy for: pulse animation, empty state, copy-report confirmation.
- Small animation spec: pulse 3s, fade 200ms, expand parent not more than 3 levels on auto-expand.

User test plan (lightweight):
- Recruit 6 backend engineers + 4 SREs. Tasks: find dominant span in 3 traces (sizes 40/300/1400 spans), compare two spans, create a short report and paste in a mock Slack. Measure task time and errors.

Notes / related links:
- Refer to "trace-ghosting-and-focus-mode-study-wip" for previous focus-mode ideas (see Drive).
- Backend ranking algorithm should re-use existing critical path code in infra/trace-aggregator (Diego to scope).

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Week 1: Align on ranking metric + wireframe review with SREs (this doc -> feedback).
- Week 2–3: Backend aggregator POC + frontend skeleton (TR-942/TR-943).
- Week 4: Internal dogfood and iterate microcopy.

Open questions for reviewers:
1) Product: agree on critical-path primary ranking?
2) Security: guidance on shareable link tokens?
3) Design: preference on panel width 300 vs 420 for compact vs detailed lanes?

Contributors: Maya (author), Avery (design), Diego (backend feasibility), Priya (accessibility review).

-- end of doc --
